analysis: The supplied units are base_text excerpts (lines 1274-2468) of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. The only PR change is test-only: head lines 807-839 add two tests, scopedMatchedSequence and translationCarriesStopScope. They exercise EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with a ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope for gpt-oss, and EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request carrying stopStringScope. The changed lines fall outside the supplied base excerpt, so the base text shows only unchanged surrounding tests: cancellation, capacity mapping, the shared KV budget, SSD staging and receipts. I reviewed these against T-041 (prefix cache, SSD tier, shared KV budget), T-010 (cancellation) and TB-007. The patch adds no production code, no new attack surface, and no change to the cache scope, TTL, encryption, or authorization behavior. The tests slightly raise coverage of stop-string handling: the scope restricts matching to the final channel, which is a behavioral correctness matter rather than a confidentiality or integrity control. Remaining open question for integration: the production changes behind these tests (ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with scope, and the cbv2Request stopStringScope parameter) are not in this batch, so I did not assess whether scoped stop-string matching could be bypassed, cause an output-truncation DoS, or leak analysis-channel content. No security regression is identified in the supplied evidence.
